about: CHAIN maldon_991 (Design/content/CHAINS.md; page Design/content/chains/maldon_991.md; words Data/writing/chain_maldon_991.json). The tribute years, 991 to 1002: Ipswich plundered and the ealdorman killed at Maldon, the first tribute of ten thousand pounds, London holding against ninety-four ships in 994, the fleet wintering at Southampton with sixteen thousand pounds and nothing to spend it on, English pennies in every purse at Hedeby, a Danish merchant with an English wife at Billingsgate, and the king's order for Saint Brice's day 1002. Fourteen cards, August 991 to 1008. Step flags ch_maldon_991_1 .. _11; side flags ch_maldon_991_paid, _bought, _ransomed, _loot, _lent, _victual, _served, _fleet, _toki, _asgot, _partner, _surety, _warned, _informer, _watched, _toki_saved, _stood_by, _blood_goods, _buried; shared spine flags en_paid_share and en_followed_silver; endings ch_maldon_991_end_north (what happened, from the Danish shore), ch_maldon_991_end_london (what happened, from the English shore) and ch_maldon_991_end_saved (history changed: changed_brice_1002_gunhild_lives). Every ending also sets ch_maldon_991_done. Every option's note names its outcome text. The word of the time for the tribute is gafol; 'Danegeld' is never used. Written 6 Oct 2026; a draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start (drawn at Gipeswic, Lundenwic or Sarre from August 991 to the end of 993). Ipswich has been plundered, Ealdorman Byrhtnoth is dead at Maldon, and the tribute is being raised on every hide. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 991 ('This year was Ipswich plundered; and very soon afterwards was Alderman Britnoth slain at Maldon', tr. Ingram 1823, read 6 Oct 2026 at avalon.law.yale.edu/medieval/ang10.asp); the tribute of 10,000 pounds on Archbishop Sigeric's counsel (same annal; chronicle_793.json 991-08-maldon); ninety-three ships at Folkestone, Sandwich and Ipswich (ASC A, under 993). That the tribute fell on the hide and that churches and thegns sold plate and land to find coin is the general picture of the later gelds (realms/england_south.md) and is assumed for 991 (?). The reeve Eadnoth (Ead- + -noth) and the woman Wulfgyth are invented. The card long.maldon.first_tribute (long_793.json) tells the same year in one card; this chain does not read its flags except long_follows_tribute in step 5. Sets ch_maldon_991_1; ch_maldon_991_paid and en_paid_share, or ch_maldon_991_bought.

cards.title: The first tribute
cards.intention: The reeve has a table set up on the strand and a list of hides. Ipswich has been plundered, the ealdorman is dead at Maldon, and the king's council has agreed to pay the fleet ten thousand pounds.

options.label: Put forty pennies toward the town's share, though no hide here is yours
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s01.out_pay

options.label: Buy the chalice the minster must sell to find its share (150 d)
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s01.out_buy (a piece worth about 240 d for 150: the first of many things sold to pay the fleet)

options.label: Pay nothing, and ask where the ships took their people
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s01.out_ask (costs nothing; the answer is Rouen)

memory.pay: paid toward the town's share of the tribute
memory.buy: bought the minster's chalice in the tribute year
memory.ask: paid nothing and asked after the taken

cards.note: Step 2 (scheduled 12 days after step 1 at Rotomagus; also drawn there to 994). People and goods of Ipswich are for sale on the quay of Rouen, a few months after the English king and the Norman duke swore before the pope's legate that neither would take in the other's enemies. Sources: the peace of Rouen, 1 March 991, made by Leo bishop of Trevi for Pope John XV, the English envoys Bishop Aethelsige, Leofstan and Aethelnoth (the pope's letter, kept by William of Malmesbury, Gesta Regum ii.166; from memory (?)); Rouen as the place where the raiders' loot and captives were sold (spine.json price_of_england, hook rotomagus; Dudo and William of Jumieges for the fleets' welcome there (?)). That Ipswich people of 991 were sold at Rouen is ours (?). The dealer, the duke's man and the fuller Leofric are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_2; ch_maldon_991_ransomed or ch_maldon_991_loot.

cards.title: Sold at Rouen
cards.intention: On the duke's quay a man of the fleet is selling eleven people on a rope and a heap of English cloth. Their speech is the speech of Ipswich.

options.label: Buy the fuller and the two women free and carry them home (150 d)
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s02.out_ransom (ransom is a good work, not a purchase: the deed is gave_alms)

options.label: Tell the duke's man what was sworn in this town on the first day of March
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s02.out_sworn_success / out_sworn_failure (doubtful; failing costs pride and the dealer's temper, nothing more)

options.label: Buy the cloth and the altar cross, and ask no one whose they were (80 d)
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s02.out_cloth (about 350 d of goods for 80; the cross can be known again)

options.label: Look, remember the faces, and walk on
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s02.out_walk (costs nothing)

memory.sworn.success: shamed the duke's man into freeing three
memory.sworn.failure: spoke of the oath and was told to mind his casks

cards.note: Step 3 (scheduled at Gipeswic 10 days after a ransom at step 2; also drawn there from 992 to 995). The town is roofing itself again; a singer has the song of the ealdorman's fight; the minster is short of coin for the next demand. Sources: The Battle of Maldon, made soon after 991 (texts_793.json maldon_991, tr. Lumsden); the herald's offer of peace for gold and the ealdorman's answer are in it and are not quoted here beyond what texts_793.json holds. A church borrowing coin to pay the fleet: Archbishop Sigeric borrowed 90 pounds of silver and 200 mancuses of gold from Bishop Aescwig against an estate at Risborough, so that the army would not burn Christ Church (charter S 882, of 995; from memory (?)). The moneyer of Gipeswic is places/gipeswic.json's Leofsige. Wulfgyth and the mass-priest are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_3; ch_maldon_991_lent.

cards.title: The song of the fight
cards.intention: Ipswich has new thatch on half its houses. In the ale-house a grey man is singing how the ealdorman stood at the causeway, and the mass-priest is waiting for him to finish so he can ask you for money.

options.label: Take what the fullers' street has gathered for you
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s03.out_thanks (turn: 100 d and eight bolts, about 244 d in all)

options.label: Lend the minster a hundred pennies against its next tribute, with no day named
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s03.out_lend (no interest: the Church forbids it; the loan comes back in ending 2 as a king's writ)

options.label: Buy the singer his ale and hear the song to the end
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s03.out_song (costs an evening; the song goes into the chest)

memory.song: heard the song of the fight to the end

cards.note: Step 4 (drawn at Lundenwic from September 994 to the end of 995; needs no earlier step and sets ch_maldon_991_1 itself, so the chain can be met here too). Olaf and Swein came to London on the Nativity of Saint Mary with ninety-four ships and the townsmen beat them off; the army then harried the coasts, took horses, and was offered tribute and food; it wintered at Southampton, fed from all the West Saxon kingdom, and was paid 16,000 pounds. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 994 ('This year came Anlaf and Sweyne to London, on the Nativity of St. Mary, with four and ninety ships', tr. Ingram 1823, avalon.law.yale.edu/medieval/ang10.asp); chronicle_793.json 994-09-08-london-attack. That the port-reeve hired merchant boats to carry the food is ours (?). The port-reeve Wulfmund (Wulf- + -mund) and the bridge-ward are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_1, ch_maldon_991_4; ch_maldon_991_victual, or ch_maldon_991_paid and en_paid_share.

ward.note: a lighterman who stood on the wall on Saint Mary's day; invented, unnamed

cards.title: London holds
cards.intention: There are scorch marks on the river wall and a burnt longship on the mud below it. London held. The fleet has gone round to Southampton for the winter, and the king has agreed to feed it and pay it sixteen thousand pounds.

options.label: Take the king's load on trust: ten sacks of flour and six casks of ale for the fleet at Southampton
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s04.out_victual (the load is the king's; it is paid for at step 5 when it is handed over whole)

options.label: Lay sixty pennies on the reeve's table toward London's share
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s04.out_share

options.label: Sell what you came to sell, and ask only what an army with silver is short of
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s04.out_clear (two true price words: drink is dear where the fleet lies)

memory.victual: took the king's food for the fleet
memory.clear: asked what the army was short of

cards.note: Step 5, the turn (scheduled at Hamwic 6 days after step 4; also drawn there from October 994 to May 995). The fleet's winter camp at Southampton: ninety-four crews with sixteen thousand pounds and a town with nothing left to sell. Olaf has gone to the king at Andover, with hostages sent to the ships, been received at the bishop's hands with the king as sponsor, and promised never again to come to England in enmity. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 994 (winter quarters at Southampton; Bishop Aelfheah and Ealdorman Aethelweard fetch Anlaf to Andover; his promise, 'as he also performed'); the treaty II Aethelred with Olaf, Jostein and Guthmund, which gives every merchant ship peace in a river mouth (lore/law_tolls.md 7.3; from memory (?)). Toke (DR 295), a merchant of Hedeby who followed the fleet to sell to it, is invented, and so is the steersman. Sets ch_maldon_991_5 and ch_maldon_991_toki; ch_maldon_991_served, or ch_maldon_991_fleet and en_followed_silver.
cards.when: moored and port.id = hamwic and ((year = 994 and month >= 10) or (year = 995 and month <= 5)) and flag.ch_maldon_991_4 and not flag.ch_maldon_991_5

toke.note: Toke Asgotsson of Hedeby, prime-signed, with a hammer and a cross on one cord; invented (name: DR 295)

chief.note: a steersman of Olaf's fleet; invented, unnamed

cards.title: The winter camp
cards.intention: Ninety-four ships lie drawn up along the Itchen under tilts. Their crews have been paid in new pennies, and Southampton has nothing left that a man could want to buy.

options.label: Hand over the king's flour and ale whole, and take the king's price
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s05.out_deliver (turn: 160 d from the king's reeve for carrying about 140 d of food)

options.label: Give the fleet first pick of your hold, and take a purse for it on top of the price
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s05.out_sell (turn: 220 d for first pick, and wine at double here for 90 days; the reeves remember who fed the fleet for gain)

options.label: Sell nothing yet. Sit by the Hedeby man's fire and learn how he talks to them
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s05.out_toke (costs an evening: half the Danish tongue and a true price word for Hedeby)

memory.deliver: handed over the king's food whole
memory.sell: gave the fleet first pick of his hold
memory.toke: sat by Toke's fire at the winter camp

cards.note: Step 6, optional (drawn at sea from 995 to 1001 after step 4). A ship of the paid fleet going home, low in the water and in a good humour. Sources: spine.json price_of_england, the sea hook ('a fleet with a tribute aboard, in a good humour'); the peace for merchant ships in II Aethelred (lore/law_tolls.md 7.3 (?)); Olaf's fleet left in 995, and the army of 997 to 1000 went to Normandy in 1000 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 1000). The ship and her steersman are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_hailed; ch_maldon_991_fleet and en_followed_silver if the player sells to her.
cards.when: under_way and year >= 995 and year <= 1001 and flag.ch_maldon_991_4 and not flag.ch_maldon_991_hailed

chief.note: the steersman of a homeward ship; invented, unnamed

cards.title: A ship going home heavy
cards.intention: A longship comes down on you under a striped sail, deep in the water for her kind. She does not shorten sail and she does not take her shields off the rail. Somebody aboard is singing.

options.label: Close and pass a cask of ale across; let them name its price
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s06.out_ale (a 10 d cask for seventy English pennies, thrown in a hat)

options.label: Heave to and ask where they will spend it
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s06.out_news (costs an hour; two true price words for Hedeby)

options.label: Bear away. A sworn peace is a long way from here
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s06.out_run_success / out_run_failure (likely; overhauled, it costs a joke at your expense and twenty pennies of 'pilot's fee')

memory.ale: sold them a cask at sea
memory.news: hove to and asked where the silver would go

cards.note: Step 7 (drawn at Sliesthorp from 995 to 1001 after step 1). English pennies in every purse at Hedeby, and King Swein striking his own, copied from King Aethelred's. Sources: more pennies of Aethelred have been found in Scandinavia than in England (spine.json price_of_england); Swein's penny of about 995, a copy of Aethelred's Crux type, signed by a moneyer Godwine 'among the Danes' (economy/silver_coin.md, the northern kings' pennies; the legend GODWINE M-AN DNER from memory (?)); the Swedish rune stones of men who 'took geld in England' are a little later (U 344, Yttergarde (?)). That the moneyer worked at Hedeby itself is not known: the mint is unplaced (?). Asgot (name: Ronninge stone), Toke's father, is invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_7 and ch_maldon_991_asgot; ch_maldon_991_fleet and en_followed_silver if the player sells into the silver.
cards.when: moored and port.id = sliesthorp and year >= 995 and year <= 1001 and flag.ch_maldon_991_1 and not flag.ch_maldon_991_7

asgot.note: Asgot, a merchant with a plot by the south jetty, Toke's father; invented

moneyer.note: an English moneyer in King Swein's pay; the coin names one Godwine (?); his face and words are the game's

cards.title: Pennies in the north
cards.intention: At Hedeby a fisherman pays for a knife with King Aethelred's head. Men home from England are buying everything twice, and by the south jetty an Englishman is striking pennies for the king of the Danes.

options.label: Take Asgot's order: eight casks of Rhenish wine before the next winter, at his price
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s07.out_order (turn: eight casks at nearly double, about 380 d over the market)

options.label: Sell into the silver: let the men home from England bid against each other
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s07.out_sell (turn: 160 d over the market, and wine dear here for 120 days)

options.label: Weigh one of the new Danish pennies against an English one, and say what you find
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s07.out_weigh (costs nothing: the news, and a true price word)

memory.order: took Asgot's order for Rhenish wine
memory.weigh: weighed the Danish penny against the English

cards.note: Step 8 (drawn at Lundenwic from 997 to 1001 after step 1). The toll rules are read at Billingsgate, and Toke of Hedeby has a house by the hythe and an English wife. Sources: IV Aethelred 2 (about 1000 (?)): a small boat a halfpenny, a larger boat with a sail a penny, a keel or hulk fourpence; the men of Rouen with wine and blubber fish; the emperor's men worthy of good laws like the Londoners (chronicle_793.json 1000-london-tolls; harbour.years_london.emperors_men in long_793.json). Danes settled in English towns as traders after the peace of 994: the charter S 909 speaks of the Danes 'who had sprung up in this island' (from memory (?)). Toke is invented; his wife Leofflaed bears a name from the will S 1462; that a Dane held a house in London in 1000 is likely and unproved (?). Sets ch_maldon_991_8 and ch_maldon_991_toki; ch_maldon_991_partner or ch_maldon_991_surety.
cards.when: moored and port.id = lundenwic and year >= 997 and year <= 1001 and flag.ch_maldon_991_1 and not flag.ch_maldon_991_8

toke.note: Toke Asgotsson, now of London; invented

wife.note: Leofflaed, a Londoner, Toke's wife; invented

cards.title: The house by the hythe
cards.intention: At Billingsgate the toll is called out by the size of the ship. Behind the hythe a Dane has built a house in the English manner, with a storehouse he cannot fill alone and a wife who keeps the tally.

options.label: Go shares in his storehouse (120 d), and take his first order
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s08.out_shares (turn: ten casks at +60%, about 480 d over the market at London's price, and a share in the house)

options.label: Stand surety for him before the reeve: your name beside a Dane's on the stick
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s08.out_surety (costs nothing now; Toke lets his own lighter carry your goods, which halves what the toll finds)

options.label: Pay your toll, eat at his table, and keep your name off other men's sticks
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s08.out_halfpenny (costs nothing)

memory.halfpenny: ate at Toke's table and signed nothing

cards.note: Step 9, the warning (drawn at Lundenwic or Hamwic from June 1001 to October 1002 after step 1). Pallig, who had the king's gold and land, has gone over to the fleet with his ships; twenty-four thousand pounds have been paid; the king has a Norman wife; and the reeve is asking which merchants deal with Danes. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle A 1001 (Pallig joined the army with the ships he could gather, 'in spite of all the pledges he had given', after great gifts of estates, gold and silver; Whitelock's rendering, from memory (?)); ASC 1002 (the tribute of 24,000 pounds through Ealdorman Leofsige; 'the lady, Richard's daughter' came in the spring; tr. Ingram 1823, avalon.law.yale.edu/medieval/ang11.asp). That reeves listed the Danes of the ports beforehand is ours (?). People: Wulfmund, Toke and the alewife are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_9; ch_maldon_991_warned, ch_maldon_991_informer, ch_maldon_991_surety or ch_maldon_991_watched.

alewife.note: the alewife by the hythe; invented, unnamed

cards.title: Who deals with Danes
cards.intention: The reeve is going from keel to keel with a clerk and a wax board. He is not asking what you carry. He is asking who you sell to, and what tongue they answer in.

options.label: Vouch for Toke: he pays his toll, hears Mass and has children baptised here
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s09.out_vouch_success / out_vouch_failure (likely; failing puts your own name on the wax board)

options.label: Say little to the reeve, and tell Toke to sell up and be over the sea before winter
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s09.out_warn (he does not go; he sends his silver and his eldest boy to Hedeby, and keeps a boat ready)

options.label: Give the reeve the names of the Danes you deal with, and take what he pays for them
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s09.out_names (60 d and an easy toll; it lasts: ending 2 pays an informer in a dead man's ground)

options.label: Say you sell wine, and everyone who has a mouth buys it
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s09.out_wine (costs nothing but his patience)

memory.vouch.success: vouched for Toke and was believed
memory.vouch.failure: vouched for a Dane and was written down
memory.warn: told Toke to be gone before winter
memory.names: gave the reeve the Danes' names
memory.wine: said he sold wine to anyone with a mouth

cards.note: Step 10, the night before (drawn at Lundenwic in October and November 1002 after step 1; the month is as near as the engine's clock comes to the twelfth of November). The king's order has reached the reeves: all the Danish men in England are to be killed on Saint Brice's mass-day. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 1002 (the king ordered slain all the Danish men who were in England, on Saint Brice's mass-day, because he was told they would take his life by treachery and then his councillors' and have his kingdom; chronicle_793.json 1002-11-13-st-brice); the charter S 909 for Saint Frideswide's, Oxford (1004), which calls it 'a most just extermination' and tells how the Danes of that town broke into the church and were burned in it (from memory (?)). Gunhild, sister of King Swein and wife of Pallig, a hostage killed in the slaughter with her husband and son, is known only from William of Malmesbury, Gesta Regum ii.177, written about 1125, and is doubted (?); that she was held at London, and everything a merchant does here, is ours. How many died, and whether any died in London, is not known (?). The danger is warned of in step 9. People: the priest Leofwine (Leof- + -wine) and Toke are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_10; ch_maldon_991_saved with changed_brice_1002_gunhild_lives and ch_maldon_991_wanted, or ch_maldon_991_toki_saved, or ch_maldon_991_stood_by.
cards.when: moored and port.id = lundenwic and year = 1002 and month >= 10 and month <= 11 and flag.ch_maldon_991_1 and not flag.ch_maldon_991_10

priest.note: Leofwine, a mass-priest who writes for the port-reeve; invented

gunhild.note: Gunhild, King Swein's sister, a hostage with her young son; historical only by William of Malmesbury's word (?)

cards.title: The king's writ
cards.intention: Two days after Martinmas is Saint Brice's mass-day. A priest who writes for the reeve comes aboard after dark, will not sit, and tells you what the king's writ says is to be done on it.

options.label: Go with Toke to the reeve's guest house, bring out the king of the Danes' sister and her boy, and drop down river on the ebb
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s10.out_gunhild_success / out_gunhild_failure (doubtful, the hard road: the door stays shut, a watchman's club and a fine of 120 d, and Toke and his sons are still got away. Success changes history and makes the house the English king's enemy)

options.label: Take Toke and his sons aboard under the tilt and sail before the bell for prime
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s10.out_toke (sure; costs the cargo space and a November crossing; Leofflaed, who is English, stays to hold the house)

options.label: Keep your men aboard, your hatch shut, and your boat where she lies
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s10.out_stay (costs nothing that can be counted)

memory.gunhild.success: carried the king of the Danes' sister out of London
memory.gunhild.failure: tried the guest-house door and got Toke away instead
memory.toke: took Toke and his sons over the sea
memory.stay: kept his hatch shut on Saint Brice's eve

cards.note: Step 11 (drawn at Lundenwic or Gipeswic from November 1002 to the end of 1003 after step 1, unless Gunhild was carried off, in which case the player is over the sea). The days after: the reeve sells what the dead owned; the news from Oxford comes down the river. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 1002; S 909, King Aethelred's charter of 1004 restoring Saint Frideswide's, burned with the Danes inside it (from memory (?)); the mass burials of young men found at St John's College, Oxford (2008) and on Ridgeway Hill, Dorset (2009) have been linked to these years, not surely (?). What was done in London or Ipswich is not recorded, and the sale of the dead men's goods is ours (?). People: Wulfmund, Leofflaed and Leofwine are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_11; ch_maldon_991_blood_goods or ch_maldon_991_buried.

cards.title: Brice's morrow
cards.intention: There are goods laid out on the hythe with nobody standing behind them: sea chests, a balance, cloaks, a child's shoes. The reeve is selling them for the king. Nobody is bidding much.

options.label: Bid for the lot: ivory, cloth and brooches at a hundred pennies
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s11.out_buy (about 360 d of goods for 100; it lasts: they are known goods, and Hedeby will know them)

options.label: Buy nothing. Give the priest thirty pennies for graves and Masses, whoever they are for
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s11.out_bury

options.label: Buy nothing, say nothing, and carry the news where it is not yet known
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.s11.out_load (costs nothing)

cards.note: Ending 1, what happened, seen from the Danish shore (drawn at Sliesthorp from November 1002 to 1006 for a player who followed the silver or carried Toke over, and did not carry Gunhild). King Swein is readying the fleet that sacks Exeter and Wilton in 1003 and Norwich and Thetford in 1004. Sources: Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 1003 ('This year was Exeter demolished, through the French churl Hugh, whom the lady had appointed her steward there', tr. Ingram 1823) and 1004; the fellowship of sworn partners, the felag, on Danish rune stones of about 1000 (DR 1 at Hedeby names a 'felagi' of King Swein's man Skarde (?)). Asgot and Toke are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_end_north, ch_maldon_991_done and one or two of unlock_partner_toke, unlock_factor_sliesthorp, unlock_ship_norse_allround_ship, unlock_plot_sliesthorp; the plain option also sets ch_maldon_991_fed_the_fleet, which the English reeves remember.
cards.when: moored and port.id = sliesthorp and ((year = 1002 and month >= 11) or (year >= 1003 and year <= 1006)) and (flag.ch_maldon_991_fleet or flag.ch_maldon_991_toki_saved) and not flag.ch_maldon_991_saved and not flag.ch_maldon_991_done

toke.note: Toke Asgotsson, if he lived; invented

cards.title: What the silver bought
cards.intention: At Hedeby they are tarring hulls in the cold, which nobody does without a reason. The king's ships go to England after the lambing. Old Asgot has a table laid in his house by the south jetty, and a reckoning to make with you.

options.label: Swear fellowship with Toke: one purse, two boats, and his father's store at Hedeby for both
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.end_north.out_felag (the honest road of this ending: 700 d and two grand rewards)

options.label: Buy the ship Asgot had built with English pennies, for what the timber cost him (300 d)
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.end_north.out_ship (a sea-going ship worth several thousand for 300 d)

options.label: Take your reckoning in pennies, and the strip of ground beside his jetty
options.note: outcome: chain_maldon_991.end_north.out_plot (900 d and a plot; the cost that lasts is ch_maldon_991_fed_the_fleet)

memory.ship: bought the ship built with English pennies
memory.plot: took his reckoning and the ground by the jetty

cards.note: Ending 2, what happened, seen from the English shore (drawn at Lundenwic from December 1002 to 1006 for any player who began the chain and did not carry Gunhild). The Danes of the port are dead or gone, their keels are not coming, and the fleet is. Sources: IV Aethelred 2.8: the emperor's men who come in their ships are held worthy of good laws like the Londoners (about 1000 (?); chronicle_793.json 1000-london-tolls); Anglo-Saxon Chronicle 1003-1004 for Swein's return. A king's writ to one merchant house is ours (?): the oldest writs that survive are of these years and are for churches. People: Wulfmund, Leofflaed and Leofwine are invented. Sets ch_maldon_991_end_london, ch_maldon_991_done and one of unlock_charter_lundenwic, unlock_plot_lundenwic (with ch_maldon_991_dead_mans_ground), unlock_factor_lundenwic, unlock_pilot_thames.
cards.when: moored and port.id = lundenwic and ((year = 1002 and month = 12) or (year >= 1003 and year <= 1006)) and flag.ch_maldon_991_1 and not flag.ch_maldon_991_saved and not flag.ch_maldon_991_done

wife.note: Leofflaed, Toke's wife or widow; invented

cards.title: An empty hythe
cards.intention: Billingsgate has room at it, which it never had. The Danish keels did not come this year. The reeve stands at the head of the hythe with his stick and counts the boats that did, and yours is one of them.

lines.when: flag.ch_maldon_991_paid or flag.ch_maldon_991_lent or flag.ch_maldon_991_served or flag.ch_maldon_991_ransomed

options.label: Ask the king's writ: your house to trade here as the Londoners do, free of the toll at this hythe
options.check: flag.ch_maldon_991_paid or flag.ch_maldon_991_lent or flag.ch_maldon_991_served or flag.ch_maldon_991_ransomed

options.label: Take what the reeve offers the man who gave him names: a dead Dane's toft behind the hythe

options.label: Keep the share in Toke's storehouse, with Leofflaed to hold the key and the tally for both houses

cards.note: Ending 3, history changed (scheduled at Sliesthorp 14 days after a success at step 10; also drawn there and at Ripa to 1008). Gunhild and her son are alive in her brother's kingdom. What really happened, if William of Malmesbury is right, is that she was beheaded after seeing her husband and son killed, and foretold that her blood would cost England dear (Gesta Regum ii.177 (?)); what really happened in any case is endings 1 and 2. Sources for what stays true: Swein had already come for tribute in 994 and comes again in 1003 (Anglo-Saxon Chronicle); a king's guest-right and protection for a foreign merchant is the ordinary form (Rimbert, Vita Anskarii, for Birka and Hedeby; Cnut's letter of 1027 for his own merchants). Invented: all the rest. Sets ch_maldon_991_end_saved, changed_brice_1002_gunhild_lives, ch_maldon_991_done, and two grand rewards from unlock_title_sweins_guest, unlock_charter_sliesthorp, unlock_ship_norse_allround_ship, unlock_partner_toke, unlock_heirloom_gunhilds_ring. ch_maldon_991_wanted (set at step 10) is the cost that lasts.
